site.name: codekite
site.summary: codekite-clone Fictional cloud CI/CD service "CodeKite CI" marketing site, focused on the pricing-page usage calculator. Pages | File | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `index.html` | Short landing: hero (YAML code example on the right), 3 feature cards, CTA to pricing | | `pricing.html` | Main page: 3 plan cards (Free / Team / Enterprise) + usage calculator (three slider+number pairs linked two-way: build minutes / concurrency / storage + ARM / macOS / GPU runner checkboxes); right-side sticky monthly total + recommended-plan badge + line-item cost breakdown; below: 16-row plan comparison table; 10-question FAQ accordion; trusted-logo row; 4-column footer | | `docs.html` | Placeholder quickstart page (one YAML example) |

explored_user_goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full codekite system, prioritizing the primary pricing flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_summary: The CodeKite pricing page offers a highly interactive and responsive usage calculator that provides immediate cost feedback, but it is undermined by significant accessibility and mobile usability flaws. All calculator inputs lack proper accessible labels, making the tool invisible to screen readers, while undersized tap targets on mobile—especially the 13x13px add-on checkboxes—create severe friction for touch users. Additionally, multiple navigation and CTA links point to dead-end placeholders (`#`), which erodes user trust and blocks goal completion.

exploration_plan.goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full codekite system, prioritizing the primary pricing flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_plan.summary: The exploration will start by traversing the landing page and adjacent navigation to establish context, then dive deeply into the pricing calculator's interactive states and edge cases. It will validate the comparison table and FAQ accordion, check the docs page, and finally repeat critical interactive checks on a mobile viewport to assess responsiveness and tap target issues.
assumptions: The pricing calculator sliders and number inputs are two-way bound and should update the sticky monthly total and line-item breakdown dynamically.
The FAQ section contains an accordion that expands and collapses on click.
Footer links and the 'Sign in' link point to '#' or are non-functional placeholders.
The recommended-plan badge on the pricing page updates based on the slider/input values.
risk_hotspots: pricing.html: Two-way binding between sliders and number inputs (risk of desync or state bugs)
pricing.html: Sticky monthly total and line-item cost breakdown accuracy when toggling ARM/macOS/GPU checkboxes
pricing.html: Missing input labels on calculator controls (flagged in prescan)
index.html: Small tap targets for navigation links (flagged in prescan)

findings.user_goal: Estimate monthly cost using the pricing calculator
findings.problem: All six calculator inputs (3 range sliders, 3 number inputs for build minutes, concurrency, and storage) lack associated <label> elements, aria-labels, or placeholders.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings consistently flag target IDs ux-7 through ux-12 as 'A form field has no label, aria-label, or placeholder.' This was observed across multiple steps on both desktop and mobile viewports.
findings.why_it_matters: Screen reader users will have no context for what these inputs control, effectively making the primary value proposition of the pricing page—the interactive calculator—completely inaccessible to them.
findings.suggestion: Add explicit, descriptive aria-labels to all range and number inputs (e.g., aria-label='Build minutes per month') or associate them with visible text labels using <label for='...'>.

findings.user_goal: Select add-on runners (ARM, macOS, GPU) on a mobile device
findings.problem: The add-on runner checkboxes have extremely small tap targets (13x13px), far below the 44px minimum mobile guidance.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings flag target IDs ux-13, ux-14, and ux-15 as 13x13px. The agent noted this 'poses a significant usability issue for users with motor impairments' and 'severely undersized for touch interaction'.
findings.why_it_matters: Users on mobile devices will struggle to accurately tap the tiny checkboxes, leading to frustration, mis-taps, and an inability to configure their estimated cost easily.
findings.suggestion: Increase the visual and interactive size of the checkboxes or wrap the accompanying text label in a <label> element to expand the clickable area to at least 44x44px.

findings.user_goal: Sign up for a trial or learn more about the company
findings.problem: Critical CTAs and navigation links, including 'Start free trial', 'Start trial', 'Talk to sales', 'Sign in', and footer links (About, Blog, Careers, etc.), point to dead-end placeholder URLs (`#`).
findings.evidence: Clicking 'Sign in' appended '#' to the URL without opening a modal or navigating. Clicking 'Blog' resulted in no visible change. DOM summary shows href='#' for these elements.
findings.why_it_matters: Users clicking primary conversion buttons like 'Start free trial' or 'Talk to sales' expect to be taken to a signup flow or contact form. Dead-end links break the conversion funnel and make the site feel unfinished or untrustworthy.
findings.suggestion: Ensure all primary CTAs link to functional pages or open appropriate modals. If pages are under construction, provide clear feedback (e.g., a modal stating 'Coming soon') rather than silently failing.

findings.user_goal: Navigate the site on a mobile device
findings.problem: Header navigation links and the logo have tap targets smaller than the 44px mobile guidance (e.g., Pricing is 47x21px, CodeKite logo is 118x28px).
findings.evidence: Layout warnings consistently flag the header navigation links (CodeKite, Pricing, Docs, Sign in) for failing the 44px height guidance on mobile viewports.
findings.why_it_matters: Small tap targets in the primary navigation make it difficult for mobile users to move between pages without accidentally tapping the wrong link, causing friction in basic wayfinding.
findings.suggestion: Increase the vertical padding of navigation links to ensure a minimum tap target height of 44px. Use CSS display: inline-block or padding to increase the interactive area without changing the visual text size.

findings.user_goal: Read FAQ answers on the pricing page
findings.problem: The FAQ accordion section is located very far down a long page, making it difficult and tedious to reach, especially on mobile.
findings.evidence: The agent attempted to scroll to the FAQ section across multiple steps (13-55) and viewports, often getting stuck or needing to scroll over 4500px down the page without successfully interacting with the accordion items.
findings.why_it_matters: Users seeking quick answers to pricing questions may abandon the page before reaching the FAQ section due to the excessive scroll depth required, increasing support burden or losing potential customers.
findings.suggestion: Consider adding anchor links at the top of the pricing page to jump directly to sections like the Calculator, Comparison Table, or FAQ. Alternatively, move the FAQ section higher on the page or into a dedicated page.

gaps: Only directly exercised 47% of visible interactive feature signatures.
